findings.current: “I am Hak Eui, a First-Generation Disciple of the Kunlun Sect. It’s an honor to meet you, Great Hero Jin Taekyung.”
findings.defect: Hak Eui omits Jin’s sobriquet from his formal introduction.
findings.rationale: 열화신룡 is part of Hak Eui’s address to Jin.
findings.replacement: “I am Hak Eui, a First-Generation Disciple of the Kunlun Sect. It’s an honor to meet you, Great Hero Jin Taekyung, the Blazing Flame Divine Dragon.”
findings.source: “곤륜파 일대제자 학의, 열화신룡 진태경 대협을 뵙습니다.”

findings.current:
“This is our first time meeting, isn’t it?”

If I hadn’t known who he was, that would have been a reasonable answer.
findings.defect: The narration reverses the condition: Jin could only say this because he knew Hak Eui’s identity. The dialogue also drops “like this,” making the meeting sound unqualifiedly their first.
findings.rationale: 모른다면 할 수 없는 대답 explicitly says the reply would be impossible without recognizing him.
findings.replacement:
“This is the first time we’ve met like this.”

I couldn’t have said that without knowing who he was.
findings.source:
“처음이군요. 이렇게 뵙는 건.”

상대의 신분을 모른다면 할 수 없는 대답이었지만

findings.current: I shrugged to show I was listening, and Hak Eui went on.
findings.defect: The shrug signals assent, not merely attention.
findings.rationale: 긍정의 의미 specifies an affirmative response.
findings.replacement: I shrugged in assent, and Hak Eui went on.
findings.source: 내가 긍정의 의미를 담아 어깨를 으쓱하자

findings.current:
had never failed to point it out when I acted unreasonably.

Though he’d always taken my side without thinking first.
findings.defect: “Never failed” makes occasional correction invariable; the next sentence loses that Jeok took Jin’s side *before* correcting him.
findings.rationale: 종종 means sometimes, and 그보다 먼저 establishes the order of Jeok’s reactions.
findings.replacement:
would sometimes remember to call me out when I acted unreasonably.

Of course, he’d take my side without a second thought first.
findings.source:
내가 사리에 맞지 않는 행동을 한다면 종종 잊지 않고 지적해 왔다.

물론 그보다 먼저 앞뒤 안 가리고 내 편부터 들고 봤지만.

findings.current: Have them quartered in front of the people.
findings.defect: Quartering is not 능지처참, execution by slow slicing.
findings.rationale: The specified method matters both to Hak Eui’s proposed punishment and to the ensuing misunderstanding.
findings.replacement: Have them executed by slow slicing in front of the people.
findings.source: 백성들이 보는 앞에서 능지처참(凌遲處斬)을 하시지요.

findings.current: even quartering them seems a little too lenient.
findings.rationale: Hak Eui continues to discuss 능지처참, not quartering.
findings.replacement: even slow slicing seems a little too lenient.
findings.source: 능지처참도 살짝 아쉬운 감이 있을 정도입니다.

findings.current: As the elders sighed, the hopeless trio stared blankly at Hak Eui, their faces vacant. Then they leaned toward each other and whispered.
findings.defect: The trio is not staring blankly at Hak Eui. They tilt their heads at the sight of *other people* staring at him.
findings.rationale: 학의를 멍하니 바라보는 사람들의 모습 is what the trio reacts to; 고개를 갸웃거리던 describes their own action.
findings.replacement: As the elders sighed, the hopeless trio tilted their heads at the sight of everyone staring blankly at Hak Eui, then whispered among themselves.
findings.source: 학의를 멍하니 바라보는 사람들의 모습에 고개를 갸웃거리던 개노답 삼형제가 쑥덕거렸다.

findings.current: “Wow, that’s the first time I’ve heard ‘quartered.’ What does that even mean?”
findings.defect: The trio’s question repeats the mistranslated name of the execution method.
findings.rationale: Cheongpung asks about 능지처참, setting up Taishan’s mistaken claim that he ate it.
findings.replacement: “Wow, I’ve never heard of ‘slow slicing’ before. What does that even mean?”
findings.source: “와, 능지처참이라는 말 처음 들어 봐요. 근데 그게 도대체 뭐예요?”

findings.current: “‘Quartered’ isn’t a dish. It’s a sobriquet.
findings.defect: Great Sir must repeat the same term Cheongpung asked about, rather than the incorrect “quartered.”
findings.rationale: His invented explanation is the next turn in the same misunderstanding of 능지처참.
findings.replacement: “‘Slow slicing’ isn’t a dish. It’s a sobriquet.

findings.current: That conversation was so absurd it was making my head spin. Just then, an old man’s voice rang out.
findings.defect: The narration drops the wordplay that turns 능지처참 into a comment on the speakers’ dismal intelligence.
findings.rationale: 능지가 처참한 echoes 능지처참 while describing the conversation as spectacularly stupid.
findings.replacement: Their intelligence had suffered a thousand cuts, and my head was spinning from listening to them. Just then, an old man’s voice rang out.
findings.source: 능지가 처참한 대화에 순간 정신이 혼미해진 내가 어지럼증을 호소하고 있던 그때

findings.current: As the severed heads fell, a tremendous roar erupted.
findings.defect: The draft changes the falling head from singular to plural.
findings.rationale: 수급 is singular here; the source does not state that multiple heads fall at this instant.
findings.replacement: As a severed head fell, a tremendous roar erupted.
findings.source: 떨어지는 수급 아래, 거대한 함성이 터져 나오고 있었다.

summary: The draft reverses a recognition cue, omits Jin’s established title, misidentifies who the trio is watching, and renders the execution method incorrectly.
